items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Thank you, Richard. Oh, I didn't tell you my name. My name is Dick Allen, commonly known as Richard.

ctx.x: What's your name anyway? My name is Al Rose. Is that your full name? No, my full name is H.N. Alphonse Delarose Lascaux. My God. I thought it was E. Albert Rose for years. Well, I actually did use that name for years for complex reasons. Where were you born? I was born in New Orleans in a 2-0 infirmary on February 3rd, 1916. Makes me 59 years old today. Just,

I'm not taking anything in any particular order. Okay. Other than happy birthday. Thank you, Richard. Oh, I didn't tell you my name. My name is Dick Allen, commonly known as Richard. Enough of this feeble attempt at you, and I'm tired. I interviewed Russell last night. Two hours of tennis and one hour of interview with Russell. It's an hour and a half. What I did with Russell. That's the D-In for a whole day. Where have you been a disc jockey? Well, I

wouldn't exactly think of myself as a disc jockey. I did, of course, run the radio show Journeys Into Jazz, which began in 1946 in Philadelphia, and is now syndicated through Southern Illinois University Radio Network. And it's just a mini-series of programs about jazz and jazz musicians on which records are played for illustration. What station was this in Philadelphia? WFIL, ABC. They had a little Eastern network that covered a lot of ABC affiliates in the area, and I had a pretty big audience back in the 40s.…
